predict.prompt: Why do prices show two decimal places?

options.label: Because a penny is a hundredth

predict.reveal: A penny is one hundredth of a dollar, so two decimal places name a whole number of cents.

cml.actionGoal: Work in the smallest place the numbers use, then decide where the point belongs for g5dc money.
invariants: A decimal is place value continued past the ones: computing in the smallest shared place turns g5dc money into whole-number arithmetic, and the point's position records which place the digits landed in.
misconceptions: Right-aligning digits instead of the points, treating a trailing zero as a change in value, or losing count of the decimal places a product carries.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the point moved one place left, how many times smaller would the amount become?

concept.body: Line up the decimal points in money amounts. You can also compute in cents, then write the total with two decimal places.
concept.narration: Line up the decimal points in money amounts. You can also compute in cents, then write the total with two decimal places.

widget.prompt: A sticker's price tag reads 24 cents. Cents are hundredths of a dollar — write the price as a decimal number of dollars.

commonErrors.feedback: That keeps the price in CENTS. Each cent is one hundredth of a dollar, so the count moves behind the decimal point, ending in the hundredths place.
That reads the cents as tenths — 2.4 would be two dollars and forty cents. A dollar holds 100 cents, so 24 of them end two places after the point.

widget.fallbackFeedback: One dollar is 100 cents, so each cent is a hundredth. Write the cents count so its last digit lands in the hundredths place.
